html:
The 2004 Equatorial Guinea coup attempt was a plot by foreign mercenaries to overthrow President Teodoro Obiang, stopped in March 2004 when their plane was seized in Zimbabwe.

The plan was led by the British former officer Simon Mann, who was buying weapons in Harare for a force of about seventy men, while an advance group waited in Malabo. It was meant to install an exiled opposition leader and was linked to backers interested in the new oil wealth.

Mann was jailed in Zimbabwe, then sent to Equatorial Guinea and later pardoned. Mark Thatcher, son of the former British prime minister, admitted in a South African court to helping pay for an aircraft. The affair hardened Obiang's grip on Malabo.
sum: The 2004 Equatorial Guinea coup attempt was a plot by foreign mercenaries to overthrow President Teodoro Obiang, stopped in March 2004 when their plane was seized in Zimbabwe.
